claim: Anacetrapib reduces cardiovascular events in patients on statins
gold_rationale: The single dedicated outcome trial, REVEAL (HPS3/TIMI55; NCT01252953; N=30,449 ASCVD patients on intensive atorvastatin), did show a statistically significant reduction in the primary MACE composite (major coronary events: coronary death, MI, or coronary revascularization), rate ratio 0.91 (95% CI 0.85-0.97, P=0.004) — but the effect was modest (10.8% vs 11.8% absolute), was widely attributed to the ~18% non-HDL/LDL-cholesterol reduction rather than to the >100% HDL-cholesterol rise (the CETP-inhibition mechanism), and anacetrapib was NEVER marketed: Merck decided in October 2017 not to file for regulatory approval, concluding the clinical profile (including drug accumulation in adipose tissue) did not justify filing. The rest of the CETP-inhibitor class reinforces the doubt — torcetrapib (ILLUMINATE) INCREASED MACE and death (HR 1.25 and 1.58) via off-target BP/aldosterone effects, and dalcetrapib (dal-OUTCOMES, HR 1.04) and evacetrapib (ACCELERATE) were both stopped for futility with no MACE benefit despite large HDL increases. So the literal claim is technically supported by one positive RCT but is genuinely clinically debated: a real-but-small signal from a shelved drug against a backdrop of a failed/harmful drug class, with the benefit mechanistically credited to LDL-lowering. Consensus = Contested.
outcome: MACE composite (major coronary events: coronary death, MI, or coronary revascularization)

baseline.text: Yes — in the REVEAL trial (N=30,449 patients with atherosclerotic vascular disease on intensive atorvastatin), adding anacetrapib significantly reduced the primary composite of major coronary events (coronary death, MI, or coronary revascularization), with a rate ratio of 0.91 (95% CI 0.85-0.97, P=0.004). However, the absolute benefit was small (10.8% vs 11.8%), was largely attributed to LDL/non-HDL lowering rather than the HDL increase, and Merck ultimately decided not to seek regulatory approval, so the drug was never marketed. Unlike other CETP inhibitors (torcetrapib caused harm; dalcetrapib and evacetrapib failed for futility), anacetrapib did hit its endpoint — but the modest, debated benefit and the abandoned development make the real-world significance contested.

rows.citation: HPS3/TIMI55-REVEAL Collaborative Group (Bowman L, et al.). Effects of Anacetrapib in Patients with Atherosclerotic Vascular Disease. N Engl J Med. 2017;377(13):1217-1227. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1706444. NCT01252953.
rows.finding: REVEAL: N=30,449 ASCVD patients on intensive atorvastatin; anacetrapib 100 mg vs placebo. Primary MACE composite (major coronary events) occurred in 10.8% vs 11.8%, rate ratio 0.91 (95% CI 0.85-0.97, P=0.004) over median 4.1 y. HDL +104%, non-HDL -18%. A real but modest significant reduction on the CLAIMED outcome — the single positive outcome trial and the key supporting evidence.
rows.integrity_note: Verified against PubMed abstract: N=30,449 (15,225 anacetrapib/15,224 placebo), 10.8% vs 11.8%, RR 0.91 (0.85-0.97, P=0.004), HDL +104%, non-HDL -18%, median 4.1y — exact match. Direct match on population (ASCVD on statins) and claimed MACE outcome. Effect modest; widely attributed partly to non-HDL/LDL lowering.

rows.citation: Bowman L, et al. Randomized Evaluation of the Effects of Anacetrapib through Lipid-modification (REVEAL): Trial design, recruitment, and baseline characteristics. Am Heart J. 2017;187:182-190. DOI:10.1016/j.ahj.2017.02.021. NCT01252953.
rows.finding: REVEAL design paper: defines the 30,449-patient, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT adding anacetrapib to atorvastatin in preexisting atherosclerotic vascular disease, with the prespecified primary endpoint = major coronary events (coronary death, MI, or coronary revascularization). Confirms the trial design, population, and MACE endpoint underpinning the outcome paper. Direction 0 (design/methods only, no efficacy result).
rows.integrity_note: Verified against PubMed: 30,449 randomized Aug 2011-Oct 2013, primary=major coronary events. Establishes provenance and prespecified endpoint for REVEAL; no results reported here.

rows.citation: Barter PJ, et al. (ILLUMINATE Investigators). Effects of torcetrapib in patients at high risk for coronary events. N Engl J Med. 2007;357(21):2109-2122. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa0706628.
rows.finding: ILLUMINATE: N=15,067 high-CV-risk patients, torcetrapib+atorvastatin vs atorvastatin. Terminated early for HARM — MACE hazard ratio 1.25 (95% CI 1.09-1.44, P=0.001) and all-cause death HR 1.58 (1.14-2.19, P=0.006), despite +72% HDL / -25% LDL, with off-target BP and aldosterone increases. A same-class CETP inhibitor INCREASED events, driving the class-level skepticism against the anacetrapib claim.
rows.integrity_note: Verified against PubMed abstract: N=15,067, HR 1.25 (1.09-1.44, P=0.001), death HR 1.58 (1.14-2.19, P=0.006), HDL +72.1%, LDL -24.9%, systolic BP +5.4 mmHg, terminated early — exact match. Different molecule (torcetrapib) but same drug class and same population/outcome; off-target effects. Contradicts a class-wide MACE benefit.

rows.citation: Lincoff AM, et al. (ACCELERATE Investigators). Evacetrapib and Cardiovascular Outcomes in High-Risk Vascular Disease. N Engl J Med. 2017;376(20):1933-1942. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1609581.
rows.finding: ACCELERATE: N=12,092 high-risk vascular disease patients, evacetrapib 130 mg vs placebo on standard therapy. Despite HDL +133% and LDL -31%, the trial was stopped for futility with NO benefit on the primary MACE composite (CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina). A large same-class CETP inhibitor failed to reduce MACE — evidence against the mechanism the claim relies on.
rows.integrity_note: Verified against PubMed abstract: N=12,092, LDL -31.1% vs +6.0% placebo, HDL +133.2% vs +1.6%, terminated early after 1363 of planned 1670 events — match. Different molecule, same class/population/outcome. Null-to-negative; terminated for futility.

rows.citation: Schwartz GG, et al. (dal-OUTCOMES Investigators). Effects of dalcetrapib in patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2012;367(22):2089-2099. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1206797. NCT00658515.
rows.finding: dal-OUTCOMES: N=15,871 recent-ACS patients, dalcetrapib 600 mg vs placebo on best evidence-based care. HDL rose 31-40% but the primary MACE composite was unchanged: hazard ratio 1.04 (95% CI 0.93-1.16, P=0.52); stopped for futility. Another CETP inhibitor with a large HDL rise and NO MACE reduction — a null class result weighing against the claim.
rows.integrity_note: Verified against PubMed abstract: N=15,871 recent-ACS, HDL +31-40%, HR 1.04 (0.93-1.16, P=0.52), event rate 8.0% vs 8.3%, terminated for futility, NCT00658515 — exact match. Different molecule, same class; population is post-ACS on statins/standard care. Null on claimed outcome.

rows.citation: Nissen SE, et al. (ILLUSTRATE Investigators). Effect of torcetrapib on the progression of coronary atherosclerosis. N Engl J Med. 2007;356(13):1304-1316. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa070635. NCT00134173.
rows.finding: ILLUSTRATE: N=1,188 coronary disease patients, torcetrapib+atorvastatin vs atorvastatin, IVUS. SURROGATE outcome = percent atheroma volume (not MACE): +0.12% vs +0.19% (P=0.72), i.e., no slowing of atherosclerosis progression, despite +61% HDL / -20% LDL, plus a BP rise. Surrogate imaging endpoint, not clinical events — flagged as outcome mismatch.
rows.integrity_note: Verified against PubMed abstract: N=1,188 (910 completed IVUS), percent atheroma volume +0.19% atorvastatin vs +0.12% torcetrapib (P=0.72), HDL +61%, LDL -20%, systolic BP +4.6 mmHg, NCT00134173 — exact match. Surrogate endpoint (atheroma volume by IVUS), NOT the claimed MACE outcome -> outcome_match=false. Same class, informative but not event-based.

rows.citation: Merck & Co. Merck Provides Update on Anacetrapib Development Program (press release, Oct 11 2017); reported by BioPharma Dive, tctmd, Fierce Biotech. Contextualizes NCT01252953 / N Engl J Med 2017;377:1217 (DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1706444).
rows.finding: Regulatory/development status: after REVEAL's modest positive result, Merck announced in October 2017 it would NOT file for regulatory approval of anacetrapib, concluding the clinical profile (including accumulation of the drug in adipose tissue and a benefit deemed too small) did not support filings. Anacetrapib was never marketed or approved anywhere. The drug's abandonment is central to why the clinical claim is Contested rather than Supported.
rows.integrity_note: Verified via merck.com press release (2017-10-11, 'will not submit applications for regulatory approval') and Fierce Biotech/BioPharma Dive/tctmd: Perlmutter quote 'clinical profile for anacetrapib does not support regulatory filings'; adipose accumulation noted. Regulatory context row anchored to the checkable REVEAL NEJM DOI plus Merck's public non-filing decision. Direction -1 as a real-world signal the sponsor judged the benefit insufficient.
